profile.constituencyprofile_Text: Gajapathinagaram Assembly Constituency Vision Action Plan has been meticulously designed to leverage the constituency's agricultural strength, dynamic industrial base, thriving construction sector, and vigorous service sector. This strategic blueprint aligns with Andhra Pradesh’s ambitious Swarna Andhra@2047 vision, which resonates with the national agenda of Viksit Bharat@2047. Gajapathinagaram Assembly Constituency was formed in 1955 and situated in the Vizianagaram district of Andhra Pradesh, India. The constituency had undergone changes in its boundaries due to delimitation exercises, with the most recent one occurring in 2008.The constituency encompasses with Gajapathinagaram, Dattirajeru, Bondapalli, Gantyada, and Jami (Part) Mandals contributions to the industries, construction, education, innovation, tourism and service sectors. These unique advantages position the constituency to achieve an ambitious annual growth target of 15% across all key sectors.
profile.geography: Gajapathinagaram Assembly Constituency is strategically located in Vizianagaram District. The constituency has rich geography, with fertile lands, water bodies, forest, and minerals. It supports agriculture, industries, and it an important region in Andhra Pradesh.
profile.populationDesc: According to the 2011 Census, the population of the Gajapathinagaram Assembly Constituency stands at 2,60,109 people, comprising 1,29,177 males and 1,30,932 females. The sex ratio is 1013 females per 1,000 males.
profile.administrationDesc: The Gajapathinagaram Assembly Constituency encompasses the mandals of Gajapathinagaram, Dattirajeru, Bondapalli, Gantyada, and part of Jami.
profile.educationHealthcareDesc: Gajapathinagaram is a rural constituency in the Vizianagaram district of Andhra Pradesh, with a semi developed social infrastructure that supports the education, healthcare, transport, and public services for its residents. School education is being strengthened with 215 Government & Private Primary schools, 28 Upper Primary Government & Private Schools, 56 High schools Government & Private, 13 Government & Private Junior colleges, 4 Government & Private Vocational colleges, 9 Government & Private Degree colleges, 1 ITI, 4 B.Ed Colleges, 1 Polytechnic College. And one Central Tribal University.The healthcare sector includes 1 Area Hospital, 7PHCs, 85 Health & Wellness Centres, with plans to reduce maternal mortality by 50%, bring infant mortality below 10 per 1,000 live births, and achieve 100% vaccination coverage.
profile.culturalheritageDesc: Gajapathinagaram Constituency is known for its rich cultural and spiritual heritage, with key attractions such as Bala Sanyasamma Thalli Temple in Gantyada mandal. It is an important spiritual and cultural landmark in the region, attracting devotees and tourists alike.The Thatipudi Reservoir plays a vital role in supporting agriculture, water supply, and overall regional development, contributing significantly to the socio-economic growth of the area.

economy_text.economy_Text: The Gajapathinagaram Constituency, with a Gross Constituency Domestic Product (GCDP) of ₹4,351 crores in 2023-24, is poised for robust economic growth, targeting ₹8,916.30 crores by 2028-29. This ambitious growth is driven by a diversified economic strategy focusing on three key sectors: Services (₹1,598.60 crores, 14.15% growth), Industries (₹887.70 crores, 17.60% growth), and Agriculture & Allied Activities (₹1,536.20 crores, 12.90% growth). By leveraging sectoral strengths, addressing infrastructure gaps, and promoting industrial diversification, the constituency aims to foster an investment-friendly environment, generate employment, and ensure inclusive and sustainable economic progress.
economy_text.gcdP_Growth_Text: Gajapathinagaram is witnessing steady economic momentum with a targeted 15% annual GCDP growth rate across key sectors like real estate, digital infrastructure, medical tourism, and agriculture. This growth trajectory aligns with the long-term vision of making the constituency a vibrant urban and economic hub by 2047.

thrust.description: Promotion of value-added agricultural products, cold storage, and supply chain infrastructure.
Development of modern dairy farms, poultry production, and processing units.
Establishment of food processing units, packaging industries, and food parks with backward linkages to farmers.
High-yield fruit, vegetable, and floriculture production with cold chain and export linkages.
Development of integrated logistics parks, transport hubs, and supply chain systems.
Smart townships, affordable housing, commercial hubs and facilitating urbanization, attracting private investment, and supporting infrastructure-led growth.
